The Marcos Collapse Has Begun: From Duterte’s Demolition to Marcos’ Demise
OPTIC Politics  |  EDITORIAL  |  September 29, 2025

The Winds Shift in Manila

The demolition campaign against the Dutertes was meant to be the signature achievement of the Marcos machine. But politics has a way of punishing hubris. What began as a crusade to neutralize the Dutertes is now spiraling into a full-blown implosion of the Marcos dynasty itself.

The Supreme Court struck down the impeachment of Vice President Sara Duterte. The Senate quickly shelved it. And then, the House of Representatives gave the nation a symbol that could not be ignored: during budget deliberations, Sara Duterte was addressed as “Her Excellency.” The OVP budget sailed smoothly through both the House and the Senate—without the toxic grandstanding, sabotage, or hostility that once defined every peso allocated to her office.

This was not mere courtesy. It was submission. It was lawmakers acknowledging the end of the demolition drive against the Dutertes. The balance of fear in Congress had shifted. The crosshairs now fixed firmly on Malacañang.

Romualdez and Co: The Fall of the Shields

The first great shield of Marcos power collapsed with the resignation of House Speaker Martin Romualdez. He tried to mask his exit as a noble gesture—“service, not retreat.” In truth, he was forced to jump before the scandal consumed him. The allegations tied to massive flood-control projects had eroded his credibility, and the pressure became untenable.

Soon after, another domino fell. Zaldy Co, Romualdez’s ally and a trusted operator, resigned. His name exploded across the nation’s headlines after MSgt Orly Regala Guteza testified before the Senate. Guteza’s testimony was devastating: suitcases stuffed with cash, delivered multiple times to Co’s residence at Horizon Towers, to Romualdez’s McKinley Street address, and finally—to a house on Aguada Street, just minutes from Malacañang’s gate.

The details were too specific to ignore. Guteza spoke of how deliveries were trimmed—forty-six luggages taken, thirty-five left behind—implying a corrupt chain of command and selective distribution. Co’s aides scrambled to deny the allegations, claiming they had no part in such activities. But the image had already been seared into public consciousness: the President’s allies, and by extension the President himself, caught in a web of suitcases filled with stolen wealth.

Institutions Crumble, Allies Retreat

Every institution tasked to hold the line for Marcos is faltering.
• The DOJ under Secretary Crispin Remulla sputters, failing to mount credible offensives. Its rhetoric is now drowned out by disbelief.
• The DPWH investigations are transparently selective, targeting the past while ignoring the stench of corruption in the present.
• The Independent Commission on Infrastructure (ICI) disintegrated when Benjamin Magalong abruptly resigned as adviser. His departure exposed the cracks, and General Rodolfo Azurin Jr. was hastily installed as a band-aid solution. The move reeked of desperation, not stability.
• Mainstream media, once relentless in demonizing Duterte, now hesitates. Editors and anchors sense the shift: the demolition narrative has lost steam. The Marcos scandals are where the fire now burns.

The demolition front that once targeted Duterte has disintegrated into a chaotic retreat.

PRRD in the Air

Amid these upheavals, whispers have grown louder: the interim release of former President Rodrigo Duterte is “in the air.” The very regime that sought to destroy him now faces collapse under its own corruption and arrogance. The irony is brutal. The more the Marcos machine tried to bury Duterte, the more it resurrected him as a figure of resilience—his image growing stronger as Marcos’ weakens.
